mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 1300K units, indicating strong demand, boosts consumer confidence, leading to increased spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer confidence
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST > 1300K, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle, increasing borrowing costs and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200K in a month, the strong labor market boosts economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances when trigger conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a quarter signals reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns after INDPRO declines are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Always-on: the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is a persistent driver of S&P 500 forward returns, with higher growth leading to positive returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns do not significantly correlate with GDP growth (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) both increase by more than 1% in a quarter, the combined effect of tightening monetary policy and rising inflation leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both increase > 1% in 1 quarter
regime_hint: monetary tightening cycle with rising inflation
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 50% of instances when trigger conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in two consecutive months signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 40% of instances when trigger conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The ratio of retail sales (RSAFS) to GDP (GDPC1) provides a persistent signal for S&P 500 forward returns, with higher ratios leading to positive returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns do not significantly correlate with the RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio (p > 0.05).
